content.value_statement: Vue projects can become hard to maintain when state, components, and rendering patterns drift. This skill gives practical Vue 3 guidance for cleaner architecture and safer performance choices.
actual_capabilities: Guides Vue 3 architecture with Composition API, script setup, and TypeScript.
Recommends component boundaries, props, emits, provide/inject, and composables.
Provides reference patterns for async components, transitions, slots, plugins, and directives.
Covers performance guidance for large lists, memoization, caching, and update hooks.
Highlights SSR-safe state management and Vue template safety considerations.
limitations: Does not run Vue builds or tests by itself.
Does not replace project-specific architecture decisions or code review.
Examples may require adaptation to existing Vue versions and libraries.
Focuses on Vue guidance, not backend APIs or deployment operations.

use_cases.title: Plan a Vue Feature
use_cases.description: Map component responsibilities, state ownership, props, emits, and composables before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Refactor Vue Components
use_cases.description: Split large components into focused views, presentational components, and reusable composables.

use_cases.title: Improve Vue Performance
use_cases.description: Apply guidance for virtual lists, memoization, caching, and avoiding expensive update hooks.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Small Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Vue best practices skill to create a typed Vue 3 component for [feature]. Include state choices and component boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Large Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Vue component and propose a refactor using focused child components and composables. Keep data flow explicit.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Rendering Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Vue list or update-heavy view. Recommend virtualization, memoization, caching, or watcher changes where appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Review Vue Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Vue feature for state ownership, SSR safety, template safety, component boundaries, and maintainability risks.

output_examples.input: Create a product filter panel for a Vue 3 catalog.
output_examples.output: A component plan with a feature container, filter controls, typed emits, derived visible products, and a reusable filtering composable.

output_examples.input: Review a slow Vue table with thousands of rows.
output_examples.output: A performance recommendation that uses list virtualization, stable item keys, realistic row heights, and targeted rendering checks.

output_examples.input: Refactor shared cart state for a Nuxt app.
output_examples.output: A state management recommendation that avoids module singletons and uses request-safe Pinia stores for SSR.

best_practices: Read the core reactivity, SFC, data flow, and composable references before implementation.
Keep route views thin and move feature logic into focused components and composables.
Optimize performance after behavior is correct, using measured bottlenecks and realistic data.
anti_patterns: Building full features inside one large route or root component.
Using updated or onUpdated for data sync that belongs in a watcher.
Adding plugins, directives, or async components without a clear product need.

faq.question: Does this skill focus on Vue 3?
faq.answer: Yes. It defaults to Vue 3, Composition API, script setup, and TypeScript.

faq.question: Can it help with Options API projects?
faq.answer: It can adapt when a project already uses Options API, but Vue 3 patterns remain the default.

faq.question: Does it include performance guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers virtual lists, memoization, KeepAlive, and safer update hook usage.

faq.question: Does it generate working code?
faq.answer: It guides code generation through architecture rules, examples, and Vue-specific implementation patterns.

faq.question: Does it replace testing?
faq.answer: No. You still need project tests, type checks, and runtime verification.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
